builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
summary: The study challenges the default of delegating subtasks to secondary LLM agents, positioning direct tool use by a single orchestrating LLM as the stronger baseline. Multi-agent delegation adds orchestration complexity and extra API calls, and the paper finds no consistent accuracy gain for that cost. Delegated pipelines can fail through distorted delegated queries, inefficient tool use, and loss of information between agents, especially on post-cutoff knowledge tasks.
rationale: Since the paper shows delegation is unreliable and sometimes harmful, the reader should A/B test direct tool use against delegation on their own workload rather than adopting multi-agent orchestration by default.

claims.statement: The study challenges the default of delegating subtasks to secondary LLM agents, positioning direct tool use by a single orchestrating LLM as the stronger baseline. Multi-agent delegation adds orchestration complexity and extra API calls, and the paper finds no consistent accuracy gain for that cost. Delegated pipelines can fail through distorted delegated queries, inefficient tool use, and loss of information between agents, especially on post-cutoff knowledge tasks.

Delegation provides no consistent accuracy improvement over non-delegated setups; for post-cutoff knowledge tasks it can substantially degrade accuracy, while direct tool use with the same LLM performs much better.
